VII, 18</cite> <he>ונֶעְסַק חד לחד וכ׳</he> and let us be engaged in dalliances in private (h. text <he>נתעלסה וכ׳</he>); a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>עֲסִיק</he>; f. <he>עָסִיקָא</he>; pl. <cite ref="P01047"><he>עֲסִיקִין</he></cite>; <he>עֲסִיקָן</he>.

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 4:15">Ib. IV, 15</cite>; a. fr.—Y. Ḥag. II, 77ᵇ <he>עד דאינון עסיקין בדידון נַעְסוֹק וכ׳</he> (not <he>עסוקין</he>) while they are occupied with their doings (songs &c.), let us be occupied with our business (study); so they sat down and engaged in discussing words of the Law.
<cite ref="Sotah 21a:11">Sot. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>בעידנא דעָסֵיק בה</he> while he is engaged in it.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 12b">B. Mets. 12ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. (<he>במאי עֲסִיקִינָן</he>) <he>במאי עַסְקִינָן אילימא וכ׳</he> what are we engaged in?, i.e. what is the case before us? Is it that the debtor admits &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 12b">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>הכא במאי עסקינן במגורשת וכ׳</he> (abbr. <he>הב״ע</he>) what is treated of here (in the Mishnah) is the case of a doubtful divorce.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 12b">Ib.</cite> <he>הכא בעבד עסקינן …</he> the slave meant in this connection is one who perforates pearls (a skillful laborer); a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 50:5">Targ. Ps. L, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 35:14">Targ. II Chr. XXXV, 14</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 25b:24">Ber. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>רב אחאי איע׳ ליה לבריה</he> Rab A. busied himself with preparations for his son’s wedding.
B. Mets. 104ᵇ יהיבנא לך לאִיעַסּוּקֵי ביה (Ms. M. לעַסּוּקֵי Pa.) I gave it to thee to do business with (but not to spend thy share for personal use); a. fr.
